claims.claim: Move given back from the high, calculated ($126.74 - $122.70 = $4.04; $4.04/$126.74)
Robinhood overnight price, Blue Ocean ATS

stories.dek: Our 06:30 edition gave Robinhood's Wednesday close as $122.28. That was wrong: two independent data providers show the shares closed at $122.70, down 1.25% on the day, and that $122.28 was not even the low, which was $122.24. The shape of the day is the part worth keeping. Robinhood opened at $122.78, climbed to $126.74 and then gave the whole move back, finishing within 46 cents of its low. A rally that is sold all the way back down usually says more about who is willing to own the shares at a higher price than any single closing number does. Watch whether the shares hold above Wednesday's low when New York opens at 14:30 UK.
stories.headline: Correction: Robinhood's Wednesday close was $122.70, not what we said
stories.short: Correction: Robinhood closed at $122.70 on Wednesday

stories.dek: US markets are shut, but the futures that trade overnight have slipped further: the S&P 500 contract is down 0.38% and the Nasdaq 100 down 0.57%, both wider than two hours ago. The cause is Wednesday's jump in government borrowing costs, and the US Treasury's own table shows where it bit hardest: three, five and seven year yields each rose 16 basis points, more than either end of the curve. That middle stretch is where the market prices how many interest rate cuts are coming over the next few years, so what got repriced is cheaper money, not a recession fear. Europe agrees: utilities, property and telecoms are falling while energy rises. Watch the US open at 14:30 UK.
stories.headline: Higher borrowing costs push stock futures lower before the US open
stories.short: Borrowing costs drag futures lower before US open

callouts.l: Desk view: buy window opens at 30

stories.dek: The VIX, the market's fear gauge, has printed in the overnight global session at 15.85, up 4.41% from Wednesday's close of 15.18. On the BuyTrigger ladder, under 15 is calm, 15 to 20 is normal, 20 to 30 is nervous and above 30 is where the system's buy window opens. So the normal band has held, and the gauge has edged further into it rather than dropping back to calm. Gold, which usually rises when people are genuinely frightened, is flat at $4,317.50. Taken together that reads as investors repricing the cost of money rather than running for cover. At 15.85 the ladder is nowhere near its buy window; the level to watch is 20.
stories.headline: The fear gauge rises again but stays inside its normal band
stories.short: Fear gauge 15.85, still in the normal band

claims.claim: US-China trade truce extended through 10 January, per Treasury Secretary Bessent
S&P 500 December futures after the announcement

stories.dek: The United States and China have extended their Busan trade truce by two months, to 10 January, announced by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent as President Xi began a state visit to Washington. A truce extension means the tariff increases both sides had threatened stay parked for now, which removes a cost that would have landed on companies importing and exporting between the two. What makes it worth noting is the reaction: futures were lower before the news and are lower still, down 0.38% on the S&P 500 contract. When a genuinely good headline cannot lift prices, something larger is setting them, and this week that something is borrowing costs. Talks continue while Xi is in the US to 25 September.
stories.headline: America and China extend their trade truce to 10 January
stories.short: US-China trade truce extended to 10 January

claims.claim: Points given back from the 06:30 level, calculated (65,859.45 - 65,513.99)
Micron overnight price, Blue Ocean ATS
Nvidia overnight price, Blue Ocean ATS

stories.dek: Japan's Nikkei 225 finished up 0.76% at 65,513.99, well below the 1.29% gain it was showing when we wrote at 06:30. It gave back 345 points into the close, and the wire Newsquawk puts the day's strength down to Japanese investors returning after a public holiday rather than fresh enthusiasm for chip shares. That matters because our earlier read treated Tokyo's bid for semiconductors as a signal the AI trade was alive somewhere. It was mostly catch-up. In the overnight US session Micron is down 0.89% and Nvidia down 0.51%, so the AI supply chain is still leaking rather than recovering. Micron reports its full-year results on 30 September, which is the next real test.
stories.headline: Tokyo's chip rally was holiday catch-up and it faded into the close
stories.short: Tokyo chip rally faded into the close

claims.claim: WTI level at the 06:30 UK edition

stories.dek: US crude for November delivery has turned positive at $92.30 a barrel, up 0.15%, after being down 0.58% when we wrote at 06:30. It is the only major market we track that is higher this morning, and it lines up with what Europe's sector tape is doing, where energy shares are rising while everything sensitive to interest rates falls. For anyone holding shares for years rather than days, a firm oil price is a double-edged thing: it helps the energy companies in a portfolio and it makes the inflation problem that is pushing borrowing costs up harder to shift. Watch whether crude holds above $92 through the US session.
stories.headline: Oil turns higher and is the one corner of the market gaining today
stories.short: Oil turns higher, the morning's one gainer
